_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals (consolidated: the company plus its 100% subsidiary Biddle Sawyer; FY = April-March since the 15-month period to Mar-2015; ₹ crore). One reported segment, so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (base business = general medicines + established vaccines vs the innovation portfolio) sits in `businessLines` and GLAXO.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash on the company's basis (cash, bank deposits and liquid mutual funds less leases: ₹2,722 cr at Mar-26) + recurring non-treasury income. Valued on P/E, as the street does. GLAXO.patch.js takes ₹718.87 cr of tax balances and long-dated provisions out of working capital (otherTreasury.base).
_revenueWhy: Built by business line (see businessLines; GLAXO.ctx.js checks the sum). FY27E +13.5%: base business +10.5% (management: base business 8-10% a year, general medicines 6-8%, vaccines double digit; FY26 lost more than ₹100 cr of general-medicine sales to the fire at a contract manufacturer (CMO), which returns in FY27, ~2.8pp; Q1FY27 standalone +15% incl. a 4-5pp soft-base effect and ~4pp from innovation) and innovation +70% (7% of Q1FY27 sales vs 4% a year earlier; Shingrix +65%; Jemperli/Zejula ramping; Blenrep launch due in Q2/Q3FY27; Arexvy approved). FY28E +10.4%: base +8%, innovation +40%. FY29E +10.1%: base +8%, innovation +30%. Below management's 12-13% a year ambition (₹8,000 cr in four to five years) and below Motilal Oswal (+14.3% FY27E, +13.3% FY28E): GSK India's revenue grew 5.5% a year in FY21-26.

businessLines._why: The company does not report revenue by business. FY26 base: innovation portfolio (Shingrix, Nucala, Trelegy, Jemperli, Zejula) ~5% of standalone revenue of ₹3,790 cr = ₹190 cr (company: 4% of Q1FY26 sales, 6% of Q4FY26 sales, ~2% like-for-like a year earlier); the rest (₹3,631.67 cr of consolidated revenue, incl. Biddle Sawyer's ₹31 cr of external sales) is the base business: general medicines (more than 80% of revenue, AR FY26; 75-78%, Q3FY26 call) and established (mainly paediatric) vaccines.

_marginWhy: EBITDA before other income: 26.3% (FY24), 31.2% (FY25), 34.3% (FY26) as gross margin rose (mix away from price-controlled products, pricing, sourcing) and selling costs fell (field-force productivity, AI tools). Q1FY27 31.5% (consolidated) with promotion deliberately front-loaded (other expenses +250bp of sales). Management (3-Aug-2026): EBITDA margin 'roughly what we were at last year in 34% kind of range' for FY27; it intends to hold margins and reinvest in launches. FY27E 34.0% (guided). FY28E 34.5% and FY29E 35.0%: operating leverage on double-digit growth, largely reinvested in oncology, haematology and liver field forces and adult-vaccine promotion; imported innovative products carry lower gross margins than locally made general medicines. Motilal Oswal models 34.6% / 37.0%.
_capexWhy: Cash capex ₹23 cr (FY25) and ₹55 cr (FY26) plus right-of-use additions (right-of-use assets rose from ₹9 cr to ₹32 cr in FY26); capital commitments ₹32.6 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 38). One owned plant (Nashik) plus ~20 contract manufacturers. We use ₹70-75 cr a year including leases.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹66.4 cr on an average gross block of ₹685 cr (Screener) = 9.7%; Q1FY27 ₹16 cr. 9.5% gives ~₹70 cr in FY27E on the engine's gross block (CWIP held flat).

otherTreasury._why: Two adjustments (GLAXO.patch.js): (a) -₹718.87 cr of tax balances and long-dated provisions taken out of working capital (current tax liabilities ₹545.99 cr less current tax assets ₹178.53 cr and deferred tax assets ₹133.85 cr, plus provisions for pricing matters ₹123.42 cr, divestment ₹1.93 cr and others, mainly indirect tax, ₹359.89 cr); the patch raises Investments by the same amount, so net cash is unchanged; (b) -₹27.37 cr of earmarked balances in Screener's cash and investments that are not treasury (unclaimed-dividend accounts ₹25.05 cr, margin money ₹1.45 cr, Clean Max equity ₹0.87 cr). Result: opening net cash = company cash ₹1,102.05 cr + term deposits ₹262.47 cr + liquid mutual funds ₹1,390.96 cr = ₹2,755.48 cr, less ₹33.27 cr of leases = ₹2,722 cr (AR FY26 notes 10, 12, 13, 18, 20).

_treasuryWhy: FY26 treasury income ₹135.77 cr (bank-deposit interest ₹56.14 cr + gains on liquid funds ₹79.63 cr; AR FY26 note 27) on a time-weighted ~₹2,500 cr (Mar-25 ₹2,498 cr, less the ₹714 cr dividend paid in Aug-2025, plus cash generated) = ~5.4%; on average year-end balances 6.5% (FY24), 6.4% (FY25), 5.2% (FY26) as the repo rate fell from 6.5% to 5.25% (held on 5-Aug-2026). The book is short (liquid funds, deposits under a year), so it reprices fast: ~5.0% on average balances for FY27-29E. The engine applies the yield to opening net cash and deducts each year's dividend in that year; in FY27 the opening ₹2,722 cr still holds the ₹966 cr FY26 dividend paid in Aug-2026, so FY27E uses 4.8% on opening (≈5.0% on the time-weighted balance); from FY28E opening cash is already net of the dividend, so 5.0%.
_otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income (AR FY26 note 27): other interest ₹0.58 cr and 'others' ₹9.00 cr in FY26 (₹0.64 cr and ₹4.90 cr in FY25; FY26 includes a ₹3.2 cr insurance claim). We use ₹7 cr. Not forecast: gains on selling property, which GSK books as exceptional items (₹20.6 cr in FY26, ₹4.7 cr in FY25). FY27E total other income ~₹138 cr vs ₹145 cr in FY26 and ₹146 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, before exceptional items): the gap is the lower yield (repo 5.25% all year) on a similar post-dividend cash balance.
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹2.7 cr (lease interest; ₹33 cr of leases at Mar-26); Q1FY27 ₹1 cr. No borrowings.
_taxWhy: Effective rate 26.3% in FY26 (26.5% before the low-taxed property gain), 26.4% in FY25 and ~26% in Q1FY27; new-regime 25.17% plus disallowances.
_payoutWhy: Dividend per share ÷ EPS: 89% (FY23, ₹32), 92% (FY24, ₹32), 99% (FY25, ₹54 incl. a ₹12 special), 93% (FY26, ₹57); FY22 ₹90 incl. a ₹60 special on the Iodex/Ostocalcium sale. No payout policy is disclosed; the parent receives 75%. We use 90%. Timing: the engine deducts each year's dividend in that year; in reality it is paid in August of the next year.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, India-only branded pharma and vaccines with an MNC parent: defensive earnings. We keep 0.8 (Ke 11.3%), the same as the other pharma initiations, rather than a lower beta that would flatter the DCF.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: the Indian pharma market grows ~9-10% in value; a long-run nominal rupee growth of 6% is below it, allowing for price control on ~40% of the portfolio.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% (base business 7-8%, innovation a rising share).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Margin creeps from 35.0% to 35.5%; launch investment absorbs most operating leverage.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1.4% of revenue incl. leases (FY26 1.4%); depreciation 1.6% (FY26 1.7%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The innovation portfolio reaches management's 10-15% of sales in FY27-28 (Shingrix in cardio-metabolic patients, Blenrep, Arexvy, bepirovirsen), general medicines grow 8-10% with no supply shocks, and margins follow Motilal Oswal's path towards 37%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: General medicines slip back to low single digits (price control on ~40% of the portfolio, generic competition in antibiotics, another supply disruption), launches ramp slowly in a self-pay market, and launch spending eats into margins.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values GSK India: P/E (Motilal Oswal 35x 12-month forward EPS, 3-Aug-2026; Nirmal Bang 50x FY27E, Aug-2025; ICICI Securities does not disclose its method). 42x = GSK India's 38.8x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before one-offs (consolidated continuing operations before exceptional items: the FY22 Iodex/Ostocalcium gain, the FY24 VRS charge and property gains are material; house sampling and median; no trough years on this basis) times the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (GSK India is outside the nine-company set, so the median of all nine names' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c; our reproduction +8.19%) = 42.0x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. The house forwardMedian on reported EPS is 37.9x because the FY22 gain (reported EPS ₹100) makes FY23-24 look like trough years (sensitivity row). No blend with GSK India's own de-rating (−13.6%) and no growth adjustment (sensitivity rows only). Bull 45.5x (75th percentile 42.2x x factor); bear 35.5x (25th percentile 32.6x x factor).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value and ignores other income. GSK India's own trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (market value less company net cash after each August dividend, over operating EBITDA before other income) has a median of 35.0x (Screener's own series 30.6x); times the EV/EBITDA factor for names outside the set (+7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c; our reproduction +7.46%) = 37.6x, rounded to 37.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 42.5x / bear 32x (75th / 25th percentile x factor).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
